title: Baked Mac and Cheese
seoTitle: Baked Mac and Cheese | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Creamy, bubbling, hall-approved mac
description: Creamy, bubbling, hall-approved mac. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Hotel pans or large baking dishes

steps.title: Par-cook the macaroni
steps.instruction: Boil elbow macaroni in well-salted water 2 minutes shy of al dente — it finishes in the oven. Drain thoroughly; wet pasta makes a soupy bake.

steps.title: Make the cheese sauce
steps.instruction: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Whisk in flour; cook 1 minute. Whisk in milk in steady streams until smooth. Simmer until thick enough to coat a spoon, then melt in cheddar and gruyere off the heat. Stir in Dijon, salt, and pepper.

steps.title: Combine pasta and sauce
steps.instruction: Fold drained macaroni into cheese sauce until every piece is coated. The sauce should look slightly loose — pasta absorbs liquid in the oven.

steps.title: Pan up and add topping
steps.instruction: Transfer to buttered hotel pans. Mix panko with melted butter and parmesan; scatter evenly over the top for a crunchy lid.

steps.title: Bake until bubbling
steps.instruction: Bake at 375°F 25–30 minutes until edges bubble and topping is deep golden. If the top browns before the center is hot, cover with foil and continue baking.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes so the bake sets — scoops hold together on the line. Serve with a spatula, not a spoon, for clean portions.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Scoop baked mac from hotel pans with a spatula so the breadcrumb lid stays intact.
Keep backup pan warming at 200°F — mac tightens as it holds; splash milk when reheating.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Creamy, bubbling, hall-approved mac. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
